source: Owner message on 2026-11-24 to the Claude session doing the UDA and Mission Control work.
owner_statement: make a rule that once usage reaches 99% work is paused at a good spot with a github handoff for my other account, unless i tell it to continue until credits run out
problem: The usage-limit rule of 2026-10-07 makes work save continuously and asks for small, restartable steps after a visible warning at about 90%, but it never says to stop. A session at 99% could start a new step that the limit then cuts off midway, leaving the other account to pick up a half-done change instead of a clean handoff.
required_behavior: At 99% visible usage, pause the work at a good stopping point unless the owner has said to continue until the credits run out.

To pause: start no new step; finish the current step only if it is small and nearly done, otherwise commit the unfinished part as work in progress, marked unfinished, and never discard it; push the work; save the checkpoint with the pause and the exact next action; end the turn with the turn-end handoff, so the work continues in another account from GitHub with one line.
The pause is an evidenced stop, not completion: the outcome stays OPEN.
When the owner has said to continue until the credits run out, keep working with the continuous saves.
The signal must be visible: a usage meter or notice the surface shows, a worker's own usage report such as Codex's session rate_limits, or the owner saying usage is at 99%. Never guess usage.
basis: docs/requirements/2026-10-07-usage-limit-continuity.owner-requirement.json and the Usage limits and account switches section of patterns/context-compaction-resilience.md before this change.
patterns/cross-account-continuity.md rule 5, which gives the one-line handoff its form.
scope: One paragraph in the Usage limits and account switches section of patterns/context-compaction-resilience.md and one sentence in its portable invariant; LESSON-INDEX.md entry 4; the two rule records that bind that text (uda.continuity.usage-warning revision 5, uda.compaction.portable-instruction revision 3); the regenerated source lock and Work handoff projection; this record; tests and fixtures.

origin.owner_outcome: At 99% usage, work pauses at a good spot with a GitHub handoff for his other account, unless he says to continue until the credits run out.

mechanism.choice: What counts as a visible signal, what a good stopping point is, and that the pause keeps the outcome OPEN.
mechanism.necessity: Most surfaces do not show usage to the worker (2026-10-07 record), so the rule triggers only on a signal that is actually visible, including the owner's own report. Defining a good stopping point as the end of a small current step, or else a marked work-in-progress commit, keeps the pause from leaving half-done work unexplained or discarding it. Keeping the outcome OPEN stops the pause being read as completion.

execution_surfaces.surface: patterns/context-compaction-resilience.md, reached through LESSON-INDEX.md entry 4 and the rule graph
Projects that copied the portable continuity invariant
execution_surfaces.reason: They pick up the new sentence when they next refresh the invariant.

nonclaims: A worker cannot see plan usage on most surfaces; where no signal is visible and the owner has not reported one, the rule does not fire, and the continuous saves remain the protection.
A static test proves the rule's text, routing and bindings, not that sessions pause at 99%; the semantic receipt stays a per-turn judgment.
